analysis.session_summary: GBP led the tape at +0.152%, USD followed at +0.098%, while NZD was weakest at -0.274%. Risk sentiment was fragile: VIX rose to 19.46367, US-Iran headlines hit late, and high-beta FX underperformed. Event reactions were unusually muted—German GDP beat, CAD GDP miss and the BOJ presser all stayed inside noise—while inline ECI still produced +0.118% USD strength. The tape reads as a choppy dollar bid with idiosyncratic GBP strength and no clean macro catalyst for most legs.

themes.theme: Risk-off pressure on high-beta and commodity FX
themes.evidence: NZD -0.274%, AUD -0.056%, VIX +1.459%; US-Iran headlines late in the window.
GBP +0.152% vs USD +0.098 and EUR +0.082; EUR/GBP -0.07%, GBP/USD +7.1 pips; no UK releases.

themes.theme: Data releases were muted, not directional
themes.evidence: German GDP beat, CAD GDP miss and BOJ presser all moved their baskets inside noise; only inline ECI still strengthened USD +0.118%.
USD intraday trough -0.175%, recovered 80%; USD/JPY +16.2 pips, USD/CHF +10.6 pips, USD/CAD +9.1 pips.

currency_drivers.USD: Inline employment cost data still drew buying; early dollar dip was recovered, closing firm.
currency_drivers.EUR: German GDP beat was muted; euro closed at best but lacked own-data impulse.
currency_drivers.JPY: BOJ press conference produced no clear move; yen rally attempt was rejected to flat.
currency_drivers.GBP: No UK releases; pound led the board while holding its range, driven by demand.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own catalysts; risk headlines left Aussie slightly softer against most majors.
currency_drivers.CAD: Soft GDP was ignored; early Canadian dollar strength faded but held small gains.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own releases; early franc weakness recovered as safe-haven demand stayed limited.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own releases; kiwi was weakest and its brief rally gave back nearly all.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped through alternating legs without a single high-confidence catalyst; the five legs netted -1.9 pips even as EUR and USD both strengthened.

polarity_reads.read: Inline 0.8% but USD still gained 0.118%; market was not positioned for USD weakness and bought any non-dovish data.
A miss at 0.0% vs 0.2% produced only a -0.010% CAD basket move; soft Canadian data failed to attract fresh CAD shorts.
A beat at 0.2% vs 0.1% drew only +0.008% EUR basket; euro upside seems exhausted or pre-priced.
High-impact event moved JPY basket just +0.028%; the yen bid was rejected, signaling no hawkish follow-through.

scenarios.name: Risk-off USD bid persists
scenarios.thesis: Middle East headlines and elevated VIX keep safe-haven dollar demand; an inline or strong ISM at 54.5 extends it.
triggers: ISM Manufacturing PMI prints at or above 54.5
scenarios.invalidation: ISM misses and VIX drops back below 19.46367; EUR/USD recovers the 61-pip down leg

pair_paths.rationale: Measured leg down of 61 pips suggests scope for the USD bid to extend; euro lacks a catalyst.
Kiwi already weakest at -0.274%; risk-off keeps shorts in control.
Measured up leg of 80.7 pips shows dollar can extend as the yen bid fades.

scenarios.name: Risk-on mean reversion
scenarios.thesis: De-escalation headlines and a softer ISM trigger dollar selling; oversold commodity FX bounce.
triggers: Iran talks progress with no new attacks
scenarios.invalidation: VIX persists above 19.46367 and USD/JPY holds above 157.783

pair_paths.rationale: Measured up leg of 31.2 pips from euro recovery; dollar unwind lifts euro.
Aussie rebound follows measured 19.5-pip up leg as risk appetite returns.
Short squeeze in kiwi after weakest close; measured 17.4-pip up leg.

scenarios.name: ISM-driven range
scenarios.thesis: ISM prints exactly in line at 54.5; no escalation; markets hold recent ranges as data remains non-directional.
triggers: EUR/USD remains inside its 69.2-pip session range
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD breaks out of its 69.2-pip session range on volume

pair_paths.rationale: Full measured session range of 69.2 pips defines likely containment if ISM is a non-event.
Measured session range of 102.8 pips reflects dollar/yen indecision.

risks.why_it_matters: They drove late risk-off moves in NZD/USD, USD/CAD and USD/ZAR and can reverse risk sentiment quickly.
Given muted event reactions so far, a surprise could be the first clean catalyst for the USD bid.
Oversized moves in USD/SEK and NZD/CHF show thin conditions can exaggerate flows.
Press conference was muted but yen had a 0.39% peak before giving back 92%; further headlines could restart the bid.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: The only scheduled release is ISM Manufacturing PMI at 16:00 (forecast 54.5, previous 54.5). Given today's muted data reactions, this is the most likely trigger to resolve the dollar bid or trigger mean reversion.
